name: integration by parts

VINIT.justification: the initial state before the product rule is applied or identified

TANCH.justification: the final boundary that encloses the transformation within specific limits

AFWD.justification: the forward operation mapping a function to its derivative

AREV.justification: the reverse operation mapping a derivative back to its primitive

CLINK.justification: the composition of two functions into a single differentiable product

IMSCRIB.justification: the self-recognition of the function as its own basis during substitution

FSPLIT.justification: the separation of the product f(x)g'(x) into the terms u and dv

FFUSE.justification: the reconstitution of the original integral from the uv product and the integral of vdu

EVALT.justification: the state where the resulting integral vdu is simpler than the original

EVALF.justification: the state where the resulting integral is more complex or divergent

ENGAGR.justification: the state where the original integral reappears within its own expansion

IFIX.justification: the permanent additive record of the indefinite integration process

phase_2.fuse_element: subtraction of the integral of v du from the product uv

phase_3.void_description: the absence of a defined functional relationship
phase_3.both_description: a self-referential integral requiring algebraic isolation

steps.domain_action: establish the existence of a product integrand within the domain
identify the internal structure of the functions f and g
apply the product rule to define the relationship between the factors
decompose the integrand into the primary term u and the differential term dv
differentiate u to obtain the differential du
integrate dv to obtain the primitive function v
confirm that the chosen u and dv lead to a simpler secondary integral
assemble the terms into the integration by parts identity uv minus integral vdu
record the constant of integration to fix the antiderivative family
apply the limits of integration to close the mathematical system

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the equality sign and algebraic substitution
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the scratchpad or register holding the values of u, v, du, and dv
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the LIATE rule determining the priority of function selection
phase_5.alfs_store: the standard table of integrals and derivatives

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational cycles required for differentiation and integration
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a solved antiderivative or numerical value
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information content of the function is preserved through the transformation
